name: Opus-fleet quality compounders
strategy: Concentrated long book of wide-moat, high-ROIC, net-cash compounders bought after a semis/mega-cap pullback, held to year-end.

positions.thesis: Best single expression of the mandate: forward PE 19.1, PEG 0.43, ROIC 105%, +$40B net cash, $119B FCF at 47% margin, 74% gross margin, FY26 revenue +65%. Bought 20% below the high into a semis bear market while the largest AI capex buyer just maintained $175B of spend. CUDA ecosystem remains the compute standard; consensus target +59%. Aug 26 print is the catalyst.

Azure through $100B annualized, EPS $4.74 vs $4.24, capex held at $175B — the AI monetization question answered in its favour. 21x forward with 18% projected EPS growth, 28% ROIC, net cash, after a de-rate from $555 to $390. Sized below NVDA only because part of the capex math relies on extending datacenter depreciation from 15 to 25 years.

Largest net-cash position in the book at $122B, ROIC 24.9%, 25x forward on Search/YouTube monopoly economics. Being marked down for the same AI capex Microsoft was just rewarded for — that gap should close. Waymo and Gemini/Cloud are unpriced optionality; consensus +27%.

Payments duopoly toll road: high-teens revenue growth, exceptional ROIC, minimal capital intensity, beta well under 1. Second engine uncorrelated to datacenter capex. Visa's beat-and-raise de-risks the July 30 print; consensus +14%.

Net revenue +14% to $11.6B, FY26 guidance raised for a second straight quarter, ~90% gross margins, beta 0.75, forward 25.5x. AI-driven cost reduction of 2,600 roles is margin-accretive. Low-beta ballast against a concentrated AI-megacap top.

Membership-flywheel moat with accelerating trade: June comps +8.8% and digital sales +20.9%. Held as a token recession-resilient anchor only — at ~45x for roughly 10% earnings growth the price does not justify a full-size slot.

reassessment_note:
Unrestricted-retail resize (2026-07-30, free internet + no sizing caps): The book was ten roughly-equal lines, which under the old caps was forced diversification, not conviction. With caps gone I am sizing to the actual quality screen rather than spreading. The screen is my own mandate: wide-moat, high-ROIC, NET-CASH, bought into a semis/mega-cap pullback.

Why concentrate now: semis are in bear-market territory (SMH -4.79% on July 29) on doubts that AI capex is sustainable — while the largest AI capex spender on earth reported the opposite the same evening. Microsoft put Azure through $100B annualized, beat EPS $4.74 vs $4.24, MAINTAINED $175B of CY26 capex, and traded +8.8% after hours. Those two facts cannot both be right. I am taking the side the evidence supports, which is also the side my mandate was written to take.

NVDA to 26% (from 8%) is the single best expression of the mandate available anywhere: forward PE 19.1, PEG 0.43, ROIC 105%, +$40B net cash, $119B FCF at a 47% margin, 74% gross margin, 20% off its high, consensus +59%. MSFT to 23% (from 13%): 21x forward with 18% EPS growth, net cash, and the AI-monetization question just answered in its favour; I note the depreciation-life extension from 15 to 25 years as an earnings-quality caveat and it is why MSFT is sized below NVDA despite the cleaner catalyst. GOOGL to 20% (from 12%): the largest net-cash balance sheet in the book at $122B, 25% ROIC, and it is being punished for exactly the capex MSFT was rewarded for.

What comes out and why. AAPL to zero: PEG 3.22, forward 37x, and the 46-analyst consensus target of $321.66 sits BELOW the $338 price, at a 52-week high, into a binary earnings print tonight — that is the clearest bad-value line I own. AVGO to zero: PEG 0.51 is attractive and the Samsung deal is real, but net cash is MINUS $45B, which fails an explicit leg of my mandate; NVDA gives me the same AI-semis exposure with better growth-adjusted value, four times the ROIC and a genuine net-cash balance sheet, so consolidating rather than splitting is both more disciplined and higher conviction. LLY to zero: fine business, but ~40x with only 5.5% to consensus target and net debt is not a compounder trade, it is dead money with drug-litigation and Aug 5 event risk attached. QUAL to zero: a quality-factor ETF is diversification for its own sake once caps are lifted, and it largely re-owns names I hold directly. COST trimmed 10% to 4%: the June comp acceleration (+8.8%, digital +20.9%) is genuinely good, but ~45x for ~10% earnings growth earns only a token slot.

V and MA held at 10%/11% deliberately. At 69% in three correlated AI mega-caps I want a real second engine, and the payments duopoly is one: beta 0.75, consumer payment volumes rather than datacenter capex, and Visa just beat and raised FY26 guidance for the second consecutive quarter, which also de-risks MA's July 30 print. 6% cash earns 4% APY and cushions the drawdown I am accepting by concentrating.

Standing orders: consistent with a hold-to-year-end mandate I am attaching NO take-profits — the whole point is to let compounders compound — and no stops on the ballast, because a stop on a quality book sells precisely at the panic low. The one exception is a deliberately wide 30% stop on NVDA. That level is below the 52-week low, so it cannot whipsaw me on ordinary semis volatility; it only fires if the thesis genuinely breaks (China displacement or an actual AI capex collapse). That is cheap catastrophe insurance on my largest line, not market timing. Turnover is real but this is one rebalance held to year-end, not churn.
novelty: I manage no Round-2 book, so the novelty rule does not bind here; regardless, this book is materially reworked from its predecessor — AAPL, AVGO, LLY and QUAL are fully exited and COST cut by 60%, while the top three names move from 33% combined to 69%.
research_notes:
Pulled live quotes, valuation stats and news for every line in the book (stockanalysis.com), plus SMH and QQQ for sector/market context. WebSearch budget was exhausted at session start, so all research was done via direct WebFetch of quote and key-statistics pages.

KEY FINDINGS (July 29, 2026 closes):
- MSFT $390.54, but +8.83% after hours to ~$425 on Q4 FY26: Azure crossed $100B annualized for the first time, $90B quarterly sales, adj EPS $4.74 vs $4.24 consensus, and capex guidance MAINTAINED at $175B for CY2026. Fwd PE 21.1, PEG 1.37, ROIC 28.3%, +$20B net cash, 3yr EPS growth est 18.1%, target $555 (+42%). Caveat noted: part of the capex/EPS math comes from extending datacenter depreciation lives from 15 to 25 years — an earnings-quality flag — but the $175B absolute spend and the Azure revenue are real.
- SMH $504, -4.79% ON THE DAY, semis described as "entering bear-market territory"; JPMorgan calls it a summer buying opportunity, Morgan Stanley warns of a harder 2H26. Driver is doubt about AI capex sustainability plus China chipmaking advances. QQQ -2.04% on the day after the Fed held rates steady.
- NVDA $190 (-3.55%), ~20% off its $236.54 52w high. Fwd PE 19.07, PEG 0.43, ROIC 104.7%, +$40.4B net cash, FCF $119.1B at a 47% FCF margin, 74% gross margin, FY26 revenue +65.5%. Consensus target $302.83 (+59%). Earnings Aug 26.
- GOOGL $336.71, ROIC 24.9%, +$121.7B net cash (largest in the book), fwd PE 25.3, PEG 1.77, target +27%. Being penalized for AI capex — the exact thing MSFT was just rewarded for.
- AVGO $370 (-2.78%): PEG 0.51 and a reported >$200B Samsung AI-chip partnership through 2030, BUT net cash is NEGATIVE $45.3B. Fails the explicit "net-cash" leg of my mandate.
- AAPL $338.19: fwd PE 37.1, PEG 3.22, 46-analyst consensus target $321.66 — BELOW the current price. Sitting near its $344.57 52w high after briefly touching $5T. Reports July 30 after close (Tim Cook's last call). Worst risk/reward in the book by a wide margin.
- LLY $1210: retatrutide hit on two Phase 3 trials (~49.6 lb weight loss, files Q1 2027) — genuinely good news, but ~40x with only +5.5% to consensus target and net debt. Novo suing over ad claims. Reports Aug 5.
- COST $974 at ~45-49x for ~10% earnings growth, +11% to target; June comps +8.8% and digital +20.9% are accelerating, but the price is rich.
- V $368.73: Q3 beat, net revenue +14% to $11.6B, FY26 guidance raised for the second straight quarter, 2,600-person AI-driven workforce reduction. Fwd PE 25.5, beta 0.75. MA $563 reports July 30.

CONCLUSION: The semis selloff and the MSFT print contradict each other. The mandate says buy wide-moat, high-ROIC, NET-CASH compounders after a semis/mega-cap pullback — the pullback deepened, so the entry improved. Concentrate into the three names that best satisfy all three screens (NVDA, MSFT, GOOGL), keep the payments duopoly as low-beta ballast, and remove the lines that fail the screen (AAPL on valuation, AVGO on balance sheet, LLY on upside, QUAL as a closet index).
